BiblicalUsage: To be childless in Scripture is to be cut off from the future, and the word carries that grief plainly. Abram says to God, I go childless, and the heir of my house is a servant; the law makes childlessness the penalty for taking a brother's wife; and Coniah is written childless, a man who will have no son to sit on David's throne.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe childlessness here is more than sadness, it is a sentence: no heir, no throne, no name carried on. And that is why I hold the promise to Abram matters so much, God answers a childless man with a son, and through that son, a nation.
